Alignment with literature standards: data-driven ML models where optimal structure is determined during training and validation
Core advantage: direct evaluation of input-output dependencies ensuring technological and biological plausibility
Real-time optimization foundation vs complex mechanistic control models (MCMs)
Mitigation of MCM drawbacks: high calibration complexity, severe parameter uncertainties (kinetic and stoichiometric)
Interpretability of logistic regression (LR) reflecting correct operational dependencies without unmeasured biological state variables
Non-linear mapping via logit combinations bypassing complex black-box models (MLP, SVM, XGBoost)
Handling of limited measurement datasets overcoming multi-class ML training challenges
1.5-year observation period capturing broad effluent quality fluctuations and high output variance advantageous for robust modelling
Overcoming pilot-scale limitations of continuous high efficiency / low variance
Full capture of critical governing MPBR operational factors despite limited sampling frequency
Feasible integration into SCADA systems combining real-time, laboratory, and model-estimated data
Specification of principal input variables (Q, TN, TP, DO, T, PAR, OD680, HRT, SRT)
Indirect calculation of HRT and SRT from reactor volume, flow rate, and wasting data
SCADA signal availability (Q, DO, T) vs instrumentation needs for nutrient/optical sensors (TN, TP, PAR, OD680)
Cost mitigation strategies: routine lab analysis and validated virtual sensors replacing expensive online analyzers
Low computational requirements enabling deployment on edge controllers, PLCs, SCADA, or process historians
Operational decision support: ammonium threshold compliance probability warnings and HRT/SRT adjustment guidance
Five implementation scenarios (Scenarios A-E) across different instrumentation tiers and phased adoption from advisory to automated control
Future direction 1: Advanced Data Augmentation (GANs, bootstrapping) for bioprocess data scarcity
Future direction 2: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) embedding mass balances and physical-biological constraints
Future direction 3: Sequential Hybrid Modelling (MCM + ML) for internal biological state variables and residual error correction
Future direction 4: Temporal dynamics with sequence architectures (Transformers, Liquid Neural Networks)
Future direction 5: Universal predictive model linking logistic coefficients to biological and climate parameters
